# std/string
String operations: length, substring, trim, split, etc.
Strings are immutable UTF-8 sequences.

Pure functions (no effects required)

## Exports

  substring(string, int, int) -> string

  toUpper(string) -> string

  toLower(string) -> string

  trim(string) -> string

    returns first index or -1

    returns true if hay contains needle

  replace(string, string, string) -> string
    replace: Replace all occurrences of old with new

  startsWith(string, string) -> bool
    startsWith: Check if string starts with prefix

  endsWith(string, string) -> bool
    endsWith: Check if string ends with suffix

  stringToInt(string) -> Option[int]
    String parsing (returns Option)

    floatToStr: Convert a float to its string representation

  intToStr(int) -> string
    intToStr: Convert an integer to its string representation

  join(string, list[string]) -> string
    join: Concatenate list of strings with delimiter

  repeat(string, int) -> string
    repeat: Repeat a string n times

  words(string) -> list[string]
    words: Split on whitespace (tabs, spaces, newlines), drop empties

  charCode(string) -> int
    Get Unicode code point of a single-character string

    foldSlices: Fold over split segments without materializing a list

  mapSlicesJoin(string, string, (string -> string)) -> string
    mapSlicesJoin: Split, transform each segment, and join results in O(n)

## Usage

# std/list
Functional list operations: map, filter, fold, etc.
Lists are immutable and backed by a flat array: indexing is O(1), and BOTH
`x :: xs` and `xs ++ ys` copy the whole list. So ANY shape that grows a list
one element at a time is O(n^2) in time: hand-written recursion,
prepend-then-reverse, and a foldl whose step conses onto a list accumulator.
foldl is O(n) only if the step is O(1); a step that conses onto (or
concatenates to) a list accumulator is O(n) per element, making the fold O(n^2).
Build lists in one pass instead:
map / filter / flatMap / zip / take   one element (or none) per input
mapAccumL                             one output per input, plus running state
foldl with a non-list accumulator     sums, counts, records, maps: always fine
Matching `[x, ...rest]` also copies `rest` on the bytecode VM, so recursion that
walks a list that way is O(n^2) there; index with nth or use a helper below.
Every pure helper below is an iterative builtin or built from one: O(n) time,
no recursion-depth limit.

Pure functions (no effects required)

## Exports

  length[a](list[a]) -> int

  head[a](list[a]) -> Option[a]

  tail[a](list[a]) -> list[a]

  reverse[a](list[a]) -> list[a]
    M-ITERATIVE-LIST: Delegates to the Go-level iterative builtin; O(n) time, O(1) stack.

  concat[a](list[a], list[a]) -> list[a]
    Appends ys to xs by copying: O(len(xs) + len(ys)) per call. In a loop, `concat(acc, [x])`

  zip[a, b](list[a], list[b]) -> list[(a, b)]
    Truncates to the shorter list. Delegates to the iterative _list_zip builtin (#1318).

  map[a, b]((a -> b), list[a]) -> list[b]
    Apply a function to each element, returning a new list.

  filter[a]((a -> bool), list[a]) -> list[a]

  foldl[a, b]((b, a -> b), b, list[a]) -> b
    Left fold. O(n) only if the step is O(1): a step that conses onto (or concatenates to)

  foldr[a, b]((a, b -> b), b, list[a]) -> b
    Right fold: foldr(f, acc, [x0, x1]) = f(x0, f(x1, acc)). Iterative builtin (right to

  mapAccumL[a, b, s]((s, a -> (b, s)), s, list[a]) -> (list[b], s)
    mapAccumL: stateful map in one left-to-right pass, O(n) for an O(1) step.

  sortBy[a]((a, a -> int), list[a]) -> list[a]
    sortBy: Sort list using a comparison function

  take[a](int, list[a]) -> list[a]
    take: Take first n elements

  range(int, int) -> list[int]
    range: the integers from start (inclusive) to end (exclusive).

  drop[a](int, list[a]) -> list[a]
    drop: Drop first n elements

  contains[a](list[a], a) -> bool
    contains: Is x an element of xs?

  nth[a](list[a], int) -> Option[a]
    nth: Get element at index (0-based). Returns None for negative or out-of-bounds.

  last[a](list[a]) -> Option[a]
    last: Get last element of list

  nth_or[a](list[a], int, a) -> a
    nth_or: Element at index, or a default if negative/out-of-bounds.

  head_or[a](list[a], a) -> a
    head_or: First element, or a default if the list is empty.

  last_or[a](list[a], a) -> a
    last_or: Last element, or a default if the list is empty.

  any[a]((a -> bool), list[a]) -> bool
    any: Check if any element satisfies predicate (short-circuits on first match:

  findIndex[a]((a -> bool), list[a]) -> Option[int]
    findIndex: Find index of first element matching predicate (short-circuits like any).

  zipWith[a, b, c]((a, b -> c), list[a], list[b]) -> list[c]
    zipWith: Combine two lists element-wise with a function

  flatMap[a, b]((a -> list[b]), list[a]) -> list[b]
    flatMap: Apply function returning list to each element, flatten results

  takeFlatMap[a, b](int, (a -> list[b]), list[a]) -> list[b]
    Fused take + flatMap: retains at most n outputs and stops invoking f once

  takeMap[a, b](int, (a -> b), list[a]) -> list[b]
    Fused take + map: retains at most n outputs and invokes f on at most n

  mapE[a, b, e]((a -> b ! {e}), list[a]) -> list[b] ! {e}
    mapE: Apply an effectful function to each element (left-to-right)

  filterE[a, e]((a -> bool ! {e}), list[a]) -> list[a] ! {e}
    filterE: Effectful predicate per element (left-to-right)

  foldlE[a, b, e]((b, a -> b ! {e}), b, list[a]) -> b ! {e}
    foldlE: Effectful left fold (left-to-right)

  flatMapE[a, b, e]((a -> list[b] ! {e}), list[a]) -> list[b] ! {e}
    flatMapE: Effectful flatMap (map then flatten, left-to-right)

  forEachE[a, e]((a -> () ! {e}), list[a]) -> () ! {e}
    forEachE: Execute effect per element, discard results (left-to-right)

  maximumInt(list[int]) -> Option[int]
    maximumInt: Find largest int in list

  minimumInt(list[int]) -> Option[int]
    minimumInt: Find smallest int in list

  maximumFloat(list[float]) -> Option[float]
    maximumFloat: Find largest float in list

  minimumFloat(list[float]) -> Option[float]
    minimumFloat: Find smallest float in list

  maximumString(list[string]) -> Option[string]
    maximumString: Find lexicographically largest string in list

  minimumString(list[string]) -> Option[string]
    minimumString: Find lexicographically smallest string in list

  member[a](a, list[a]) -> bool
    member: Check if element is in list (argument order flipped vs contains).

  dedup[a](list[a]) -> list[a]
    dedup: Remove duplicates, preserving first occurrence order

  intersect[a](list[a], list[a]) -> list[a]
    intersect: Elements present in both lists

  union[a](list[a], list[a]) -> list[a]
    union: Combine two lists without duplicates

  difference[a](list[a], list[a]) -> list[a]
    difference: Elements in first list but not in second

## Usage

  -- or --
  import std/list as List
